decided.question: does an archived topic keep a rename control on screen, or is the archived rename a route allowance only
decided.chose: the archived row draws no rename control; the route still renames an archived topic, for a caller holding its id, and a curator who wants the name changed on screen restores it, renames it and archives it again
decided.rejected: drawing a rename control on the archived row, and the justification that correcting a spelling must not require restoring the topic — which the screens made false
decided.why: rule 3 — the narrower screen refuses more and adds no control, and the contracts and TC-02-E2E-01 already draw the archived row with restore alone
decided.recordedAt: the 'archived | rename' row of the State Machine table in specs/requests/02-request-topics.md, which now carries the decision and the rejected alternative; the transition's observer is TC-02-INT-22, which renames the topic it archives and asserts the new name is written and survives the restore

decided.question: does the staff seed carry the four topics the request named, or the nine that also cover the retired access kinds

decided.recordedAt: the Decided under the Seed Data table in specs/requests/02-request-topics.contracts.md, which now names the reversal cost on both sides beside the rationale and the rejected alternative

decided.question: which catalogue read fills the requests list's topic filter, now that REQ-02-011 removes an archived topic from the active read
decided.chose: the filter is filled from GET .../request-topics?status=all with each archived entry marked archived, while the new-request picker reads status=active
decided.rejected: filling both controls from one read, which hides the requests raised under an archived topic from the control that finds them
decided.why: rule 1 and rule 2 — TC-02-E2E-03 already asserts the filter offers the archived topic and returns its request, and REQ-02-011 already scopes the removal to the active read; the rule was stated nowhere but inside that case

decided.question: which message answers a topicId that is both archived and of the wrong audience
decided.chose: REQUEST_MESSAGES.topicUnavailable — the audience is compared only on a topic REQ-02-019 has already found active, so an archived topic answers topicUnavailable whatever its audience
decided.rejected: comparing the audience on any row the id names, which leaves one body answerable either way
decided.why: rule 3 — the refusal that scopes more narrowly is the one that never discloses the audience of a topic the caller may not use, and REQ-02-019 already answers one message for every unusable topic
